slides.title: Dispatch Copilot: launch it inside a Pro plan, not as an add-on

paragraphs.text: Dispatch Copilot: launch it inside a Pro plan, not as an add-on
Discussion document for the CEO and executive team, January 2027 planning
Brightwork
CEO and executive team
Synthetic benchmark data; every number from the briefing pack
Executive summary
Launch Copilot in Q2 2027 inside a Pro plan at $12 more per seat with a usage allowance, not as a $149 add-on, then start the mobile rewrite
Copilot is worth launching, but its productivity and competitive gains are smaller than they look
–	Beta accounts gained 11% in jobs per dispatcher-hour, against 2% for matched ones
–	Losing ground to Routewise costs at most 109 deals a year, and a discount overlaps it
As a $149 add-on it would bring about $2.5M of ARR, not the $8M planned, and attract the costliest users
–	Only 14% of beta accounts paid $149; 46% of survey respondents said they would
–	Buyers ran 1.9 times the mean account's requests; inference takes 41% of their price
A Pro plan at $12 more per seat adds about $2.9M of ARR and, with an allowance, keeps margin above 75%
–	If 33% of accounts move up, as to the 2023 tier, Pro adds $2.89M of ARR
–	A 500-request allowance per seat holds company gross margin at 76.3%
The real cost is a two-quarter mobile delay: the rewrite must follow at once, watched by four gates
–	Mobile drives 27% of churn against 6% for AI; the delay risks up to about $1.1M of ARR
–	If Pro take-up halves, 105% NRR needs the rewrite to cut mobile churn by about 40%
